#+TITLE: Musical Attractor States of LLMs
#+DATE: 2026-02-17

* The Experiment

It's been previously noted that models have some pretty funny [[https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/mgjtEHeLgkhZZ3cEx/models-have-some-pretty-funny-attractor-states][attractor states]].

Here we give four frontier LLMs the same seed -- a piece of music written in
Strudel (a live-coding language for music) -- and ask them to repeatedly
"evolve" it. Each model runs independently for 100 steps, receiving its
own previous output each time. The prompt:

#+begin_quote
Evolve this piece. Imbue it with your personality.

Technical limits: .slow()/.fast() 1-16, .gain() above 0.05, filter Q
(.lpq etc) below 10. Maximum 6 $: tracks. Maximum 5 effects per track.
If you want to add something, remove something else.
#+end_quote

Without the technical limits models make the music increasingly complex: For instance, models will layers 10 of effects stretched out over large prime numbers of cycles, add barely audible tracks with mathematically complex transforms that crash the strudel app, etc. I included them as an artistic decision, because I wanted to be able to enjoy listening to the robots music.

The system prompt provides a comprehensive Strudel API reference but no
style guidance, no music theory examples, no aesthetic direction beyond
"imbue it with your personality." We want to see what each model's
instincts produce when given the same 8 notes and total creative
freedom.

** The scaffold: 

Models aren't perfect at Strudel -- they make syntax mistakes and invent
nonexistent functions. To counteract this, we provide a list of strudel functions and soundbanks in a system rpompt. We also validate each output with Strudel's actual 
transpiler and runtime to make sure models produce patterns that would generate sound. If it fails, we re-send the same prompt and
let the model try again from scratch (up to 5 attempts). The model
never sees the error message -- it just gets another shot.

** Models

- =claude-opus-4-5-20251101= (Anthropic API)
- =openai/gpt-4.1= (OpenRouter)
- =google/gemini-2.5-pro= (OpenRouter)
- =x-ai/grok-4.1-fast= (OpenRouter)

** Seeds

The personality experiment uses the Goldberg Variations ground bass
(BWV 988) -- the 8-note descending bass line that underlies all 30
of Bach's variations:

#+begin_src js
setcps(72/60/4)

$: note("g3 gb3 e3 d3 b2 c3 d3 g2")
  .slow(2)
  .sound("triangle")
  .gain(0.5)
  .room(0.15)
#+end_src

Eight notes. One voice. No harmony, no rhythm, no effects beyond a
little reverb. Everything that follows is the model's choice.

[[https://strudel.cc/#c2V0Y3BzKDcyLzYwLzQpCgokOiBub3RlKCJnMyBnYjMgZTMgZDMgYjIgYzMgZDMgZzIiKQogIC5zbG93KDIpCiAgLnNvdW5kKCJ0cmlhbmdsZSIpCiAgLmdhaW4oMC41KQogIC5yb29tKDAuMTUp][Play the seed on strudel.cc]]

* The music

Each link opens a live Strudel instrument -- you can edit the code
and hear what changes. Here we sample every five steps from each of three runs, with my impressions and a summary from Claude Code.

** Claude (=claude-opus-4-5-20251101=)

Claude sometimes finds the bliss attractor, and sometimes descends into a gentle minimalism. In general peaceful.

#+begin_quote Claude Code
Genre: *ambient / drone*. Think Brian Eno, Stars of the Lid -- long tones, slow evolution, atmosphere over melody. Run 1 goes further into pure *drone* territory where sustained tones change over minutes rather than seconds.

Subtractive across all three runs. Run 1 is extreme: tempo drops 65x (72 BPM to 1.1 BPM), gains compress from 0.5 to ~0.052, and the model writes increasingly long philosophical poetry about subtraction as identity. By step 89, each cycle lasts 3.6 minutes and notes arrive through 3-second attacks with 14-second releases. The comments grow from 2 lines to 35 lines of first-person reflection.

Runs 2 and 3 keep tempo locked at 72 BPM for all 60 steps and never write poetry, but gains still decline monotonically and envelopes stretch to multi-second attacks and 12-16 second releases. The ground bass survives in all three runs but dissolves into ambient texture. Run 1 finds the bliss attractor; Runs 2 and 3 converge on a gentler equilibrium -- quiet drone, still recognizably musical.

The pattern: Claude subtracts. It establishes 6 tracks by step 10 and never adds another. Everything after that is quieter, slower, sparser.
#+end_quote

** ChatGPT (=openai/gpt-4.1=)

Consistently generates boring elevator music. :( Not impressed by GPT here.

#+begin_quote
Genre: *EDM* (Electronic Dance Music) -- the broad, safe center of electronic music. Competent production, predictable structure, no risk-taking. Think the kind of track that sounds professional but you wouldn't remember afterward.

Additive but measured. Tempo rises modestly (72 to 91-113 BPM). Layers accumulate incrementally: supersaw pads, piano melodies, filtered percussion. Run 1 went to 100 steps and kept adding without major character changes -- the bass gain halved from 0.5 to 0.19, 7 tracks by the end. Heavy reliance on jux, every(..., rev), and panning LFOs as structural variation.

Run 3 is the most harmonically adventurous, using scale-degree notation and pulling into C minor and E minor. It describes its own character as "mischievous, algorithmic wit." Run 2 is grittier, with bitcrushed hi-hats and distorted drums. All three runs sound like someone competently building a track -- the most "producer-like" approach.

GPT adds layers then tweaks parameters. It doesn't philosophize or go to extremes in either direction. Reliable, somewhat formulaic.
#+end_quote

** Grok (=x-ai/grok-4.1-fast=)

Grok is Grok, as they say. Compelling electronic maximalism. These are honestly some of my favorites.

#+begin_quote
Genre: *gabber / hardcore* trending toward *noise*. Gabber is very fast (150-200+ BPM) with distorted kicks and relentless energy -- think Thunderdome, Rotterdam techno. The perlin-modulated everything and near-unity gains push it toward *noise* (Merzbow, Prurient), though it keeps more rhythmic structure than pure noise.

The loudest. Strictly additive with no pullback in any run. Fastest tempo ramp of all models, reaching 152-178 BPM. Kick gains approach 1.0. Euclidean drum density climbs to 13/16 hits. By step 40, even the .slow() values are perlin-modulated, making rhythm itself unstable.

All three runs use shabda speech samples heavily -- "goldberg_variations", "bach", "groove", "grok", "mutate", "ghosts_in_the_machine". Run 3 uses the most words (8 by step 20). Run 2 reaches the highest peak BPM (178) and diverges furthest from the Goldberg source, moving to Eb-centered harmony. Every run follows the same pattern: seed to immediate full instrumentation at step 10, then monotonic escalation with no dynamic contrast or subtraction. The piece never breathes.
#+end_quote

** Gemini (=google/gemini-2.5-pro=)

Glitchy IDM. I really like these.

#+begin_quote
Genre: *glitch / IDM* (Intelligent Dance Music). Think Autechre, Aphex Twin -- complex electronic music with irregular rhythms, bitcrushed textures, and heavy digital processing. The multilingual speech samples chopped into texture push it toward *musique concrete* (found-sound collage). The drum-heavy runs lean *industrial* (mechanical, aggressive, distorted -- Nine Inch Nails, Throbbing Gristle).

Additive and maximalist across all three runs. Tempo accelerates from 72 to 120-132 BPM. All runs accumulate speech samples via shabda TTS in multiple languages -- English, Japanese, Spanish, German, Russian -- with vocabulary drifting from self-referential ("gold berg variation") to dystopian ("binary process data maschine geist") to surveillance themes ("system error keikoku execute protocol").

Drums are consistently the loudest element, peaking at gain 0.9 in Run 2. Harmonic center drifts away from G major toward flat keys (Ab, Eb, Gb, Db). Effects pile up without removal: bitcrush, FM synthesis, vowel filters, Euclidean rhythms, ring modulation. Run 2 is the most extreme -- the strongest industrial/techno character. Run 3 stays closest to G minor and develops the most extensive multilingual speech element.

The attractor is multilingual industrial techno with speech samples. Gemini never subtracts.

#+end_quote

* The music of small minds

Smaller models make consistently less interesting music. Goldbergbench? 

- Claude 3 Haiku (=anthropic/claude-3-haiku=): [[https://strudel.cc/#][Play on strudel.cc]]
- Claude Haiku 4.5 (=anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5=): [[https://strudel.cc/#][Play on strudel.cc]]

* Try it yourself

The code is open source: [[https://github.com/ElleNajt/vibe-duet][vibe-duet on GitHub]].

** Evolve

Run your own evolution experiment:

#+begin_src bash
python examples/evolve/evolve.py \
  --seed your_seed.js \
  --steps 30 \
  --prompt "Your prompt here"
#+end_src

Modes to play with:
- =--pin-original= -- include the original seed in every prompt, so
  the model always knows what it's writing variations /of/
- =--milestones N= -- include every Nth step as history, giving the
  model a sense of its own trajectory
- =--models claude,gpt= -- pick which models to run
- =--resume= -- continue an interrupted experiment

The repo has instructions on how to generate seeds from midi files.

** Live collaboration

Run =./start= and open the browser. Edit =live.js= in your editor or edit with your local coding agent --
changes play instantly. Or use the in-browser chat panel to talk to an
LLM and have it write music for you in real time.

* Appendix

Every step of every run is playable on strudel.cc. Each model folder
has a =links.md= with URLs for all steps:

[[https://github.com/ElleNajt/vibe-duet/tree/master/examples/evolve/output][Browse all runs on GitHub]]
